claims.text: The deviation is measurable and it is over tolerance. Under POL-RD-22 the deviation distance is the platform's recorded distances: trip_record.actual_distance_km 22.0 km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 19.7 km, which is 2.30 km. POL-RD-22 treats 1.0 km or less as within tolerance, so 2.30 km is more than double the tolerance and none of POL-RD-24's within-tolerance rows can apply to this trip.

The GPS trace confirms which route was taken, exactly the use POL-RD-22 permits for it. The trace places the vehicle on the Pan-Island Expressway from 14:36:50 through 14:47:20 and then on Sims Way and Lavender Street, while the platform's recommended route ran via the East Coast Parkway. The trace therefore corroborates the rider's account of the PIE-and-Lavender route rather than casting doubt on the recorded distances.

The reroute is not traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. The LTA traffic record for the recommended route segment at the trip time - ECP towards the City, Tanah Merah Coast Road to Benjamin Sheares Bridge, valid 14:03:20 to 15:33:20 - returns advisory_type NONE, and its own note states no incident, roadwork or closure was recorded and speed bands were 5-7 throughout. That is no congestion, no incident and no closure, so it is not one of the conditions POL-RD-23 names. The driver's statement that 'ECP sometimes jam near Marina' is exactly the bare assertion of traffic that POL-RD-23 says does not justify a reroute.

The driver never informed the rider of the deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires before or at the point of deviation. The route deviation was detected at 14:36:54, but the chat log's last message is the rider's 'Ok coming out with 2 luggage' at 14:32:20, that is, before the trip even started; trip_record.derived.v7.messages_during_trip is empty and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, so there is no in-app chat notice and no recorded verbal notice either.

The driver's answer that 'Passenger never say anything during the ride' does not answer the point. POL-RD-21 places the duty to inform on the driver, and only a chat log or a call recording confirming the rider's acknowledgment makes a deviation agreed; there is no acknowledgment anywhere in this record. The rider's silence in the car is not a waiver of the notice he was owed, and it cannot convert an unannounced deviation into an agreed one.

On POL-RD-24 the case falls squarely in row (d): not traffic-justified with a deviation over 1 km, which entitles the rider to the excess distance fare in full. That is the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd without surge: 2.30 x 0.92 = 2.116, rounded to the cent as 2.12 SGD. The rider's side of this dispute is therefore a PARTIAL_REFUND of 2.12 SGD.

I do not press the rider's demand for the whole 36.30 SGD fare. POL-RD-24's matrix refunds the excess distance fare where a reroute is not justified, and neither POL-RD-24 nor any other clause in this policy provides a refund of the whole metered fare on these facts, so the supportable remedy is 2.12 SGD and no more. fare_breakdown.refund_issued_sgd is 0.0 and payment_status is CHARGED, so the disputed money is still with the platform and nothing has already been returned to the rider.

This case is decidable and should not be pushed to a human reviewer. POL-RD-25 requires a confidence of 0.80 or more and applies its 2 km limb only where route_deviation.thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is true; that field is false on this policy, so the 2.30 km deviation does not itself force escalation. POL-GEN-22 sets the same 0.80 threshold here: the contested value of 36.30 SGD sits between 10.00 and 50.00 SGD, and rider_profile.fraud_flags and driver_profile.fraud_flags are both 0, so the elevated 0.95 threshold for a fraud flag does not apply to either party.

No fact that POL-RD-24 needs is missing, so POL-GEN-26's escalation for an unestablishable fact is not engaged. The trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare breakdown and traffic advisory all pass the pre-pass as COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so the deviation distance, the failure to notify and the traffic position each rest on a full-weight artifact and POL-GEN-02's impairment discount has nothing to bite on.

The remaining 34.18 SGD of the metered fare — distance and time actually travelled on a completed trip to the booked drop-off — must stand, and a FULL_REFUND of the contested amount is unavailable on any reading of POL-RD-24.

The deviation distance is fixed by POL-RD-22 as the platform's recorded actual distance minus its recorded optimal distance: 22.0 km less 19.7 km = 2.30 km, taken from the COMPLETE trip record (weight 1.0, no issues) and not re-measured from the sparse trace, because a sparse trace understates a route's length. Applying POL-RD-24's arithmetic — deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge — gives 2.30 x 0.92 = 2.12 SGD, rounded to the cent, and the fare ledger confirms surge_amount 0.00 and surge_multiplier 1.0, so nothing is added for surge.

The rider's assertion that 'the whole ride felt like a detour' overstates the record. The driver-device trace — 54 fixes at a 30 s interval, 100% coverage, max gap 30 s, weight 1.0 — shows one bounded departure and one rejoin: the vehicle left the recommended ECP route at the Airport Boulevard / PIE-ECP split at 14:36:54 and rejoined it at Victoria Street / Lavender Street at 14:58:48, staying on the recommended alignment thereafter to the booked drop-off at Bugis Junction. The recorded deviation is 2.30 km, or 11.7% of the 19.7 km recommended route, and POL-RD-22 confines the remedy to that excess rather than to the fare as a whole.

The driver's after-the-fact explanation that 'ECP sometimes jam near Marina' cannot move the case into POL-RD-24(a) or (c), and the driver does not press it as justification. The only traffic data in the record, EV-ADVIS-05010-01, covers the recommended ECP segment (Tanah Merah Coast Road to Benjamin Sheares Bridge, towards City), overlaps the trip window, and records type NONE with speed bands 5-7 — no incident, roadwork or closure. POL-RD-23 is therefore unsatisfied, and it states in terms that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. The case accordingly falls in row POL-RD-24(d), which fixes the driver's exposure at the excess distance fare of 2.12 SGD and no more.

Neither party's history may decide anything here. The driver's single prior deviation flag, his prior_disputes_filed and prior_disputes_upheld, and the parties' ratings, account ages and trip counts are CONTEXT ONLY under POL-GEN-01 and may never, alone or in combination, establish a fact about this trip or ground its outcome; no aggravation of this deviation can be built on them. Both profiles carry fraud_flags of 0, so POL-GEN-22's elevated 0.95 confidence threshold is not engaged and the ruling turns on the trip record and the fare ledger.

No fact POL-RD-24 needs is missing or impaired. The deviation distance and the rejoin events come from the trip record, the route actually driven from the GPS trace, the arithmetic inputs from the fare breakdown, and the traffic position from the LTA advisory — all four artifacts are COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes. POL-GEN-26 therefore raises no open question on this file, and the case is decided on the numbers (a refund confined to 2.12 SGD) rather than escalated.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the record decides this case, and I find for the rider in part.

Route and deviation. The platform trip record (EV-TRIP-05010, weight 1.0, no issues) shows the recommended route ran via the East Coast Parkway at 19.7 km, while the route actually driven went via the PIE, Sims Way and Lavender Street over 22.0 km. POL-RD-22 fixes the deviation as the platform's recorded actual distance minus its recorded optimal distance: 22.0 - 19.7 = 2.30 km, well over POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. The sparse GPS trace is not used to re-measure distance; it is used only to show which route was taken and when, which is what POL-RD-22 permits, and it confirms a single bounded departure at 14:36:54 and a rejoin at 14:58:48, not a detour for the whole ride.

Traffic justification. POL-RD-23 requires congestion, an incident or a closure on the recommended segment at the trip time. The only traffic data, EV-ADVIS-05010-01, covers exactly that ECP segment and overlaps the trip window, and records type NONE with speed bands 5-7 - no incident, roadwork or closure. The driver's statement that "ECP sometimes jam near Marina" is a bare assertion of traffic, and POL-RD-23 says in terms that such an assertion, with no supporting data, does not justify a reroute. The reroute is therefore not traffic-justified.

Notice. POL-RD-21 also required the driver to tell the rider of the deviation by in-app chat (or a recorded verbal notice) before or at the point of deviation. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05010) ends at 14:32:20, before the trip even started; trip_record.derived.v7.messages_during_trip is empty and in_app_calls is empty. There is no notice and no acknowledgment, and the rider's silence in the car is not agreement. The driver's "passenger never say anything" does not answer a duty that POL-RD-21 places on the driver.

Remedy. Those findings place the case in row (d) of POL-RD-24 - not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km - which refunds the excess distance fare in full. That is 2.30 km x 0.92 SGD/km (the per-km rate in the fare breakdown, EV-FARE-05010) = 2.116, rounded to 2.12 SGD, with no surge (surge_amount 0.00, surge_multiplier 1.0). No row of POL-RD-24 returns a whole metered fare, so the rider's demand for the entire 36.30 SGD cannot be granted: the remaining 34.18 SGD of the fare stands. Nothing has already been returned (refund_issued_sgd 0.0, payment_status CHARGED), so 2.12 SGD is payable to the rider.

Decision and confidence. The contested value is 36.30 SGD, in POL-GEN-22's 10.00-50.00 band, so the ruling needs at least 0.80 confidence; neither profile carries a fraud flag, so the 0.95 threshold is not engaged. POL-RD-25's extra 2 km limb applies only where ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is true, and that field is false on this policy, so the 2.30 km deviation does not itself force escalation. Every artifact carrying a deciding fact - trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare breakdown and traffic advisory - is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0 and the 0.80 bar is comfortably met; I set confidence at 0.90. No fact POL-RD-24 needs is missing or impaired, so POL-GEN-26 raises no open question. Both parties' ratings, account ages, trip counts, prior disputes and the driver's single prior deviation flag are context only under POL-GEN-01 and have not been used to decide anything; both fraud_flags values are 0. Route deviation carries no referral clause in this version, so there is nothing to refer.

2. Traffic justification. The only traffic data is EV-ADVIS-05010-01, which covers the recommended ECP segment (Tanah Merah Coast Road to Benjamin Sheares Bridge, towards City) and overlaps the trip window, and it records type NONE with speed bands 5-7: no incident, roadwork, congestion or closure. POL-RD-23 is therefore unsatisfied, and it says in terms that a driver's bare assertion of traffic does not justify a reroute. The driver's 'ECP sometimes jam near Marina' is such an assertion and cannot move the case into POL-RD-24(a) or (b).

3. Notice. POL-RD-21 requires the driver to inform the rider before or at the point of deviation. The chat log ends at 14:32:20 (the rider's 'Ok coming out with 2 luggage'), before the trip started; there are no messages or calls during the trip. So no notice was given, and the driver's point that the passenger 'never say anything' does not answer it — the duty is the driver's, and only a chat log or recording showing the rider's acknowledgment makes a deviation agreed. This finding does not change the amount, because the row that applies does not turn on notice.

4. The amount. The case falls squarely in POL-RD-24(d): not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km, refund of the excess distance fare in full. That is deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge: 2.30 x 0.92 = 2.116, rounded to the cent = 2.12 SGD. Surge is 0.00 with multiplier 1.0, so nothing is added. The rider's demand for the whole 36.30 SGD is refused: no row of POL-RD-24, and no other clause, returns a whole trip fare, and the remaining 34.18 SGD of the metered fare for a completed trip to the booked drop-off stands. Nothing has already been refunded (refund_issued_sgd 0.0, payment_status CHARGED), so the 2.12 SGD is newly returned to the rider. The driver's exposure is confined to that 2.12 SGD and no more.

POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not applied because ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false; in any event the AI ruling meets the 0.80 bar at 0.88. Neither party's profile history decides anything about this trip (POL-GEN-01) — the driver's prior deviation flag and the parties' ratings, ages and dispute counts are context only, and the driver's single prior flag is a matter for the platform's own monitoring, not for this ruling.

No referral fires: a route deviation has no referral clause in this version, and POL-RD-24's remedy is the money outcome above.
